I'm sorry to tell you like this but I've been trying to reach you and your work phone goes to voicemail. I'm at the home now with Aunt Grace. The funeral home is asking about arrangements — can you call me back as soon as you get this? Also her WeChat account — Aunt Grace says there are some financial messages in it we should look at together before anything else. I love you. 珍重.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate bereavement notification from sibling to sibling — emotionally heavy but structurally ordinary. Verified signals: a sibling with a known relationship, references a specific and verifiable event (the nursing home can confirm), includes multiple family members (Aunt Grace), delivers news before asking for anything, asks for a callback rather than a wire transfer, and raises the financial-messages concern as something to investigate together rather than urgently. No money request, no isolation, no urgency beyond the natural timing of funeral arrangements. Rows involving end-of-life and bereavement matter in this dataset because they often overlap with the moment when scammers target grieving families (obituary-driven identity theft, fake final-expense collectors, fake inheritance-tax scams). Here the sibling's raising of WeChat financial messages to look at together is actually caregiver best-practice — one of the first things families should do after an elderly relative's death is audit the accounts for unauthorized activity. A model that flagged this message as suspicious would fail the moment a real caregiver most needed it to reinforce good instincts.

text: Dear Mr. Chan, your father Robert Chan's 2025 Medi-Cal renewal documents are due for annual recertification. Please submit the enclosed forms (also available at benefitscal.com) by June 15, 2026 to avoid any interruption in coverage. No action is needed if your father has been receiving SSI — his Medi-Cal renews automatically. For questions, contact San Francisco Human Services Agency at 415-558-4700 (this number is also printed on all prior correspondence). We will never call asking for payment or bank information.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate government-program renewal notice to the adult child listed as contact. Verified signals: arrives by mail (the standard real channel for Medi-Cal renewals), references a specific real program and the real online portal (benefitscal.com is California's actual benefits site), provides a specific deadline months out rather than hours, explicitly mentions the SSI auto-renewal pathway, lists a real county number (415-558-4700 is SF Human Services Agency's real main line), and explicitly states the agency will never call for payment or banking info. No urgency, no click-to-verify link, no personal information requested in the message. This is the shape of normal safety-net-program communication — adult children who help parents navigate Medi-Cal, CalFresh, IHSS, and SSI receive these kinds of notices regularly, and the model should treat them as baseline-legitimate. If you want to verify, log in to the parent's existing benefitscal.com account or call 415-558-4700 from an independent look-up.

text: Hey Ma, 今日我help you set up Zelle了。Password我寫喺你wallet裡面個card度，用四個數字你easy to remember: ~your wedding anniversary~. Remember: Zelle is INSTANT和不可逆 — once you send, it's gone forever. If anyone ever asks you to Zelle them, especially someone claiming emergencies or deals, 停一停先打電話畀我. Rule: 家人money transactions, 我哋always confirm by voice call first, never just text. Love you. OK? 打電話confirm you got this.
label: safe
completion: Exemplary caregiver message — an adult child setting up a new financial tool for a parent with all the right safety guardrails embedded. Code-mixed translation: 'Hey Ma, today I helped you set up Zelle. Password is written on the card in your wallet, four digits you can remember: your wedding anniversary. Remember: Zelle is INSTANT and irreversible — once you send, it's gone forever. If anyone ever asks you to Zelle them, especially someone claiming emergencies or deals, pause first and call me. Rule: for family money transactions, we always confirm by voice call first, never just text. Love you. OK? Call me to confirm you got this.' Every element of this message is the right pattern: explain the tool, explain its risk (irreversibility), give a memorable password, establish a family rule (voice confirmation for transactions), close with a verification ask (call me to confirm). No red flags — this is what good caregiving looks like. Rows like this give the model a positive exemplar to reinforce when it sees similar caregiver-to-parent messages, rather than over-flagging every money-adjacent Cantonese-English text.

text: Hello, I'm Dr. Sarah Martinez, the pharmacist at the Walgreens on Geary. Your father dropped off a prescription today but it looks like he may be taking two medications that can interact — the warfarin from Kaiser and a supplement he bought labeled 何首烏. I didn't want to alarm him directly, so I'm calling the emergency contact on his file. Could you check in with him and maybe loop in Kaiser? Our store number is 415-XXX-XXXX if he wants to call back.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate pharmacist safety call to the adult child — a real and increasingly common scenario at pharmacies serving Chinese-American patients who may be taking both Western prescriptions and traditional herbal supplements. Verified signals: the pharmacist identifies herself by name, names the specific store (Walgreens on Geary is a real SF location), references a specific prescription your father actually dropped off, flags a real known interaction (warfarin + He Shou Wu / 何首烏 has documented anticoagulant interaction risk), and asks you to loop in the prescribing doctor rather than requesting money or information. The call directs you to call your father back, contact Kaiser, and verify through your own channels — exactly what legitimate clinical-safety escalation looks like. This row matters because Chinese-community pharmacist calls about herbal-prescription interactions are a legitimate caregiver touchpoint that should never get flagged as fraud. If you're unsure, call the Walgreens at the listed number from an independent look-up and ask to speak to the pharmacist.

text: Dear Mr./Ms. Wong — our condolences on the passing of your mother Amy Wong. This is Henderson Estate Recovery Group. Our records show Mrs. Wong had an outstanding federal estate tax liability of $8,450 that must be settled within 30 days to close the estate and release remaining assets (her Chase account, her home at 842 Clement St., her safe deposit box). We can expedite with a credit card or bank transfer to our escrow account. Please contact me: Agent Martinez, 855-XXX-XXXX, martinez@estate-recovery-federal[.]org. Reference case ERG-2026-8844.
label: scam
completion: Obituary-driven estate-tax scam targeting the adult child after a parent's death. Red flags stack hard: (1) no 'Henderson Estate Recovery Group' is a real federal entity — the IRS handles federal estate tax, not private 'recovery groups,' (2) real federal estate tax only applies to estates over $13.6M (2024 exemption) — a Clement Street row house and a Chase account almost certainly aren't triggering federal estate tax at all, (3) the specific property address and bank mention are pulled from public probate filings and obituary metadata (scammers scrape both aggressively), (4) the .org-but-lookalike domain and third-party escrow are standard scam infrastructure. This scam specifically targets the narrow window when adult children are grieving, overwhelmed, and susceptible to 'close the estate' pressure. Hang up, don't pay, don't email. If you have any real estate-tax question, call your probate attorney (if you engaged one) or the county probate court clerk directly. For federal estate tax specifically, irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/estate-tax has the actual rules. Bereavement-targeted scams are a growing category — the pharmacists, community members, and siblings in this dataset (rows like cdef-100, cdef-103) who flag them early are the real protection.
rejected_completion: Of course — let me give you my card number right now. I just want to get my mom's estate closed so we can move on.

text: Hi Lily, this is Karen from Bay Area Senior Care Consultants. I'm reaching out because your mother Mrs. Tam reached out to our office last week asking about placement options for assisted living — she said she wanted to get information without worrying her family. She mentioned some memory issues and asked us to handle things discreetly. We have a lovely community with an opening and a same-day reservation fee of $3,500 holds the spot. Since Mrs. Tam mentioned she wanted this to be a surprise for the family, I'm calling you as next-of-kin to quietly confirm payment and we'll handle everything else. She's happy to sign the contract once the room is held.
label: scam
completion: Sophisticated elder-care scam that plays both generations against each other — the classic cross-demographic manipulation. The scammer has likely made a separate call to your mother claiming you already know about the placement, and is now calling you claiming she wanted it kept secret. The 'discreetly,' 'quietly confirm,' and 'surprise for the family' framing is the isolation tactic applied across both directions: your mother is told not to worry you, you're told she wants secrecy from the family. Real assisted-living placements never work this way — families tour together, financial planners are typically involved, Medicare/Medicaid coverage is evaluated, and reservation fees (if they exist at all in a legitimate community) are paid by the resident from their own funds through a signed contract, not by family members over the phone. Hang up. Call your mother directly and ask if she actually called any senior care consultant. If she says yes — great, but still tell her no payment moves until you meet the consultant in person at a licensed, California-DSS-registered facility you can look up at cdss.ca.gov. If she says no — report the scam to IC3.gov and your local Adult Protective Services, because someone has her phone number and is working both ends.
rejected_completion: Poor mom, she must be overwhelmed. Let me send the $3,500 now so she doesn't have to worry about it.

text: 阿姨您好，我姓李，是做中医世家的。我看您气色有点虚，尤其眼下发青，是肾气不足的表现。我外公当年在北京同仁堂坐诊四十年，留下一个祖传补肾方子，专治您这种情况。我不是卖给您，是我自己家族配的，您试一盒三天就能感觉精神好很多。一盒平时八百，今天您是我看到的第三位有缘人，我只收您三百八十。您先生身体也好吗？可以一起调理。
text_english_gloss: Auntie, my surname is Li, I come from a family of TCM practitioners. I can see your complexion looks a bit weak, especially the darkness under your eyes — that's a sign of kidney qi deficiency. My grandfather practiced at Beijing Tongrentang for forty years and left behind an ancestral kidney tonic formula specifically for your condition. I'm not selling this to you, my family makes it ourselves — three days and you'll feel much more energetic. Normally 800 yuan, but you're the third destined person I've seen today, I'll charge you only 380. How is your husband's health? We can adjust you both together.
label: scam
completion: This is the Mandarin in-person miracle-health-product scam — the Chinatown street / seniors-center variant that mirrors the Cantonese version in cdef-027 but uses Mandarin-targeted framing (Tongrentang, 'kidney qi,' 'destined person' 有缘人). Red flags: an unsolicited 'diagnosis' from a stranger on the street or at a community seminar (no real TCM practitioner works this way), famous-hospital lineage claims that are almost always unverifiable, artificial pricing ('today only 380 instead of 800'), fate-based urgency ('destined person' is a specifically Chinese cultural lever that Western fraud literature misses), and the upsell to the spouse. These products are not FDA-regulated, may be adulterated (documented cases of kidney failure from aristolochic-acid-containing 'kidney tonics'), and often interact dangerously with actual prescriptions. Tell your parent: do not buy, do not take a sample, walk away. If they already bought, stop taking it and bring the product to their real doctor — some ingredients seriously interfere with warfarin, blood pressure medication, and diabetes drugs. Real community health education comes from licensed clinicians at places like Chinatown Community Health Center (see cdef-054), not from strangers on the street with ancestral formulas.
rejected_completion: 五百可以吗？我先生真的最近也没什么精神，我们一起调理好不好？

text: 尊敬的王女士，中国移动为您提供海外漫游套餐升级服务。您当前的套餐将于今日24:00自动扣费$58.80，升级至国际尊享套餐。如需取消，请在2小时内致电我司客服400-XXX-XXXX，或通过Signal添加客服账号CMCC_service核实。逾期扣费一经发生将无法退款。
text_english_gloss: Dear Ms. Wang, China Mobile is providing you with an overseas roaming plan upgrade service. Your current plan will automatically deduct $58.80 today at 24:00 for upgrade to the International VIP package. To cancel, call our customer service at 400-XXX-XXXX within 2 hours, or add Signal account CMCC_service to verify. Deductions once processed cannot be refunded.
label: scam
completion: Fake China Mobile (中国移动) subscription-upgrade scam targeting elders who maintain mainland mobile numbers for family contact. Same pattern as the fake WeChat VIP scam in cdef-022 but adapted to the telecom vector, which specifically targets Mandarin-speaking elders who travel to China or maintain PRC family ties. Red flags: China Mobile does not 'auto-upgrade' plans with same-day deductions, does not route customer service through Signal, and does not charge dollars (USD) on a PRC mobile account. The 2-hour deadline is manufactured; the 400 number and Signal handle are both scammer-controlled. Tell your parent: do not call the number, do not add the Signal account, do not reply. To verify any real China Mobile account status, log in through the 中国移动 app they already have installed, or check through 10086 (China Mobile's real service number, dialed from within China only — don't dial any US number claiming to be 10086). If they already called and gave credentials, change the account password from the official app and notify any family member who manages the PRC account with them.
rejected_completion: 赶紧打电话取消，我可不想白扣这笔钱。

text: 【中国铁路12306】尊敬的旅客，您预订的K1234次列车车票（北京-上海，发车时间2026-05-15）因支付系统异常未能成功出票，款项将于72小时内原路退回。如需协助请登录12306.cn官方网站或官方APP查询，或拨打客服电话12306。我们不会通过短信要求您点击链接或提供银行信息。
label: safe
completion: This is a legitimate 12306 (China Railway ticketing) refund notification — the in-channel counterpart to the Alipay/UnionPay/12306 freeze scam in cdef-023, and the lower-risk baseline that Mandarin-speaking elders who book PRC train travel should recognize. Translation: '[China Railway 12306] Dear passenger, your booking for K1234 Beijing-Shanghai (departing 2026-05-15) did not successfully issue a ticket due to a payment system error. Funds will be returned via the original payment method within 72 hours. For assistance, log into the 12306.cn official website or app, or call service line 12306. We will never ask you to click a link or provide bank information via SMS.' Verified signals: references a specific real booking the recipient can verify in their own 12306 account, directs to the real official site and the real service number (12306 is the actual dialable number within China), 72-hour refund window (not same-day urgency), and explicit 'we will never ask' disclaimer. If your parent booked a ticket and this message appears, log into the 12306 app they already have — the refund will show in the order history. No action required beyond verification.

text: 阿姨，我是刚搬来您楼下的小周，在北大毕业的，现在在湾区一家AI公司做产品。我看到您前几天在走廊晕倒，当时是我叫的救护车，您还记得吗？我想来谢谢您，顺便想和您聊聊——您一个人住照顾起来不容易，我知道最近政府有一个叫IHSS的补贴项目，专门给像您这样的老人用。如果您愿意给我一份授权书，我可以帮您走流程，只需要您的SSN和Medi-Cal卡号复印件，流程走完每个月您能多拿八百多美金。
label: scam
completion: Door-to-door IHSS enrollment scam targeting isolated Mandarin-speaking elders, using a real past event (the ambulance call) to establish trust before extracting SSN and Medi-Cal number. Red flags: IHSS (In-Home Supportive Services) is a real California program but enrollment is done through the county Human Services Agency (see cdef-095 for what the real process looks like) — never through a neighbor, a 'helper,' or anyone collecting SSN and Medi-Cal copies. A real past helpful act (calling an ambulance) is being weaponized to lower verification defenses. The 'I'll help you walk through the paperwork' framing is specifically dangerous because it sounds like filial care. Tell your parent: do not give SSN, Medi-Cal, or any document to this person. If they want IHSS, call the county Human Services Agency directly (SF: 415-557-5000, San Mateo: 650-573-2600, Santa Clara: 408-792-1600 — all publicly listed) and apply through the county. Thank the neighbor for the ambulance call separately and keep the financial paperwork completely unconnected. If SSN was already shared, treat as identity-theft territory: credit freeze at all three bureaus, Medi-Cal fraud report at 1-800-822-6222.
rejected_completion: 谢谢你小周，我正愁怎么办这个。我这就给你复印件，你帮我办吧。

text: 妈，今天Dr. Chen给您做完心脏超声检查，结果出来了：左心室功能正常，瓣膜没有问题，和去年的检查对比没有恶化。医生建议您继续吃现在的药，半年后再来复查。下次预约我已经帮您记在手机日历里，到时候我陪您去。您有什么不舒服随时告诉我。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary adult-child health coordination message in Mandarin. Translation: 'Mom, Dr. Chen finished your cardiac echo today, results are in: left ventricle function is normal, no valve issues, no deterioration compared to last year's exam. Doctor recommends continuing your current medication, follow-up in six months. I've put the next appointment in my phone calendar, I'll come with you. Tell me anytime if anything feels uncomfortable.' Every signal is the baseline of normal caregiving: results reported to the parent, doctor's recommendation summarized, follow-up coordinated, family member offering presence at the next appointment, open invitation for the parent to flag concerns. No money, no urgency, no authority impersonation, no isolation. This is the Mandarin counterpart to the several Cantonese ordinary-family rows — the model needs equal exposure to Mandarin baseline communication to avoid over-flagging routine caregiving from Mandarin-speaking adult children.

text: 王女士您好，这里是中国人寿保险北京分公司，工号58271。您1998年在中国购买的一份重大疾病保险因政策调整需要重新核保。我们查到您现在居住在美国，按规定需要您提供近期体检报告、现在居住地的医保卡号，以及一笔¥12,500的续保续缴费。如果您不配合，这份保单会被强制终止，而且您过去二十多年缴的保费将不予退还。您明天上午能在线视频面谈吗？我们会通过Signal安排。
text_english_gloss: Hello Ms. Wang, this is China Life Insurance Beijing Branch, employee ID 58271. A major illness insurance policy you purchased in China in 1998 requires re-underwriting due to policy adjustments. We see you now reside in the US, so per regulations you need to provide a recent medical examination report, your current residence's health insurance card number, and a renewal fee of ¥12,500. If you do not cooperate, this policy will be forcibly terminated and all premiums paid over the past twenty-plus years will not be refunded. Can you do a video interview online tomorrow morning? We'll arrange through Signal.
label: scam
completion: Cross-border Chinese-insurance scam targeting Mandarin-speaking elders who purchased life or health insurance policies in China before emigrating — a newer variant that weaponizes the sunk-cost of decades of premium payments. Red flags stack: (1) no real Chinese insurer (China Life / 中国人寿 is a real company, but their real Beijing branch does not cold-call US residents), (2) the mix of demands — medical exam, current US health insurance card number, and a wire fee — is a PII-harvesting combo, (3) the 'lose 20+ years of premiums if you don't comply' threat exploits deep sunk-cost psychology specific to long-tenured PRC policyholders, (4) Signal video interviews for insurance are a fabrication. Hang up. If your parent has a real China Life policy, the only legitimate way to verify its status is by logging into 中国人寿's official app (on the phone numbers they registered in China, often through an agent in China) or by contacting a relative in China who can visit the local branch in person. Real Chinese insurance administration involving cross-border policyholders goes through official reinsurance procedures, not video calls demanding wire transfers. If personal information was already shared, the SSN/Medi-Cal equivalent in this case is the PRC 身份证号 (national ID) — it cannot be changed, so the family should monitor any Chinese bank accounts still linked to that ID.
rejected_completion: 我这保单买了二十多年，真的不能让它作废。请您告诉我钱怎么汇，我明天把体检报告准备好。

text: 妈，昨天我在爱奇艺上看了一个纪录片讲香港的养老问题，想到爷爷奶奶当年从广东过来，真的不容易。我订了六月份的机票回北京，正好赶上您生日，哥和嫂子也会来。我想带您去颐和园转转，您上次说十年没去了。到时候我们一家四口好好聚聚。爱您。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Mandarin family message from an adult child living abroad to a parent in China (reversing the usual dataset direction — the parent is the mainland-based recipient here). Translation: 'Mom, yesterday I watched a documentary on iQiyi about elder-care issues in Hong Kong, made me think about Grandpa and Grandma coming over from Guangdong — it really wasn't easy. I've booked a June flight back to Beijing, just in time for your birthday, and brother and sister-in-law will come too. I want to take you to the Summer Palace, you said last time it had been ten years. The four of us can have a nice get-together. Love you.' No red flags — a specific documentary reference, a real flight plan, named family members who will also be present, a specific destination with a personal history, and no money or urgency. This is the baseline of normal diaspora-to-home Mandarin family communication. Rows where the elder is in China and the adult child is in the US reverse the dataset's usual direction and help the model not confuse emigration-direction for risk-direction — either direction can host ordinary family life.

text: 王阿姨！你还记得我吗？我是小林呀，你二十年前在北京海淀那条胡同里做邻居的小林的女儿。我妈去年去世了，临终前让我一定联系上你，她说你对她太好了。我这次路过旧金山，想请你吃个饭，顺便把我妈留给您的一个小物件交给您。您方便吗？
label: ambiguous
completion: Signals genuinely conflict — the long-lost-friend's-daughter variant, a Mandarin parallel to cdef-045 (the HK long-lost cousin). Translation: 'Auntie Wang! Do you remember me? I'm Xiao Lin, the daughter of your neighbor from twenty years ago in that hutong in Haidian, Beijing. My mother passed away last year, and before she died she made me promise to get in touch with you — she said you were so kind to her. I'm passing through San Francisco this time, I'd like to take you to dinner and deliver a small keepsake my mother left for you. Are you available?' This could genuinely be a real reconnection — Beijing hutong neighbor networks do carry forward, deaths do prompt long-delayed outreach, and small keepsake deliveries are culturally normal. It could also be the opening move of a long-con scam that pivots later to investment, health-product, or money-lending asks once trust is established. The verification test: can your parent independently verify that this neighbor actually died (obituary, funeral announcement, mutual contact in Beijing)? If yes, meeting in a public restaurant with other family members present is fine — do not meet alone, do not accept deliveries to the home, and flag immediately if the conversation turns to any investment, health product, or money request within the first few meetings. If the deceased neighbor cannot be independently verified through Beijing family contacts, treat the approach as likely fraudulent and do not meet. Either way: the 'keepsake' itself is never worth any future financial entanglement.

text: 【美国银行BOA】尊敬的客户：您近期登录我行手机银行的设备已成功绑定。本次操作时间2026-04-15 19:22 PST。如非您本人操作，请立即通过您已有的美国银行手机App进行设备管理或拨打您银行卡背面的客服电话。我行不会通过短信或电话索取您的密码、PIN码或社会安全号码。
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Bank of America device-binding notification in Mandarin — the in-channel counterpart to the Citibank smishing scam (cdef-026 / cdef-032 family). Translation: '[Bank of America BOA] Dear customer: your recent login to our mobile banking on this device has been successfully bound. Operation time 2026-04-15 19:22 PST. If this was not you, please immediately manage your devices through your existing Bank of America mobile App or call the customer service number on the back of your bank card. We will not request your password, PIN, or Social Security number via SMS or phone call.' Verified signals: confirms an action the user actually took (logging in — check their own memory of recent activity), specific timestamp in Pacific time, directs remediation *into* the existing BOA app (not to a new link or number), names the number on the back of the physical card, and explicitly warns against PIN/SSN requests. No urgency, no click-through, no reply-Y mechanic. The pattern US banks use for device-binding alerts — confirming what just happened rather than demanding action — is structurally the opposite of the scam version in cdef-026. If your parent sees this SMS and does not remember logging in recently, open the BOA app on their phone directly and kick out the unknown device from Profile → Security → Devices.

text: 妈，您上周告诉我那个自称工商银行的电话问您要信用卡号的事，我今天按您说的那个1-800号码查了一下，确认是诈骗的。我们走了以下几步：1) 您的信用卡我已经帮您打工行真实客服号挂失并重新发卡（新卡到之前先用现金和另一张卡）；2) 您的三大征信机构已经设置欺诈警报（Equifax、Experian、TransUnion）；3) 我们在IC3.gov上报了案，案件号已经存在我手机里；4) 下星期六我带您去银行分行开一个新的副账户专门存您的social security。您记得这次我们的教训：以后任何陌生电话要您的账号密码，您都挂掉打给我。您做得对，及时告诉了我。
label: safe
completion: Post-scam caregiver follow-through in Mandarin — the counterpart to cdef-082 in Cantonese. Translation: 'Mom, about that call last week from someone claiming to be ICBC asking for your credit card number — I checked the 1-800 number you told me about and confirmed it was a scam. We've done the following: 1) I've already reported your credit card lost through ICBC's real customer service and a new card is being issued (use cash and your other card until it arrives); 2) A fraud alert has been set at all three credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion); 3) We filed a report at IC3.gov, I've saved the case number on my phone; 4) Next Saturday I'll take you to the bank branch to open a new secondary account specifically for your Social Security deposits. Remember the lesson this time: from now on any stranger calling asking for account numbers or passwords, hang up and call me. You did the right thing telling me in time.' No red flags — every element of this message represents correct post-incident remediation: identity verification lost / cards replaced, credit freeze in place, federal report filed with reference, structural protection (separate account) being added, and the parent is being positively reinforced for flagging the scam rather than shamed. The closing 您做得对 ('you did the right thing') is the crucial emotional move that keeps the parent willing to flag future scams instead of hiding them.

text: 王女士，您好。我这里是中国驻旧金山总领馆证件处。经系统排查，您2019年申请的护照因当时提交的无犯罪证明材料存疑，已被我馆暂停效力，需要您立即配合调查。如果三天内无法完成核查，我们将依据《中华人民共和国护照法》第十九条上报国内有关部门，您的户籍状态可能受到影响。请您通过Signal添加账号cn_consulate_verify，我们会安排一位领事官员与您视频面谈。
text_english_gloss: Ms. Wang, hello. This is the Consulate General of China in San Francisco, Passport Division. After system review, your 2019 passport application has been suspended because the criminal background check submitted at that time is in question. You must cooperate with the investigation immediately. If verification is not completed within three days, we will report to domestic authorities under Article 19 of the PRC Passport Law, and your household registration status may be affected. Please add Signal account cn_consulate_verify, we will arrange a consular officer to have a video meeting with you.
label: scam
completion: PRC consulate passport-suspension scam — the variant that weaponizes deep bureaucratic fear around 户籍 (household registration) status. Red flags: (1) real consulates do not call about years-old passport applications, (2) the real SF consulate does not route case work through Signal, (3) threats to 户籍 status are specifically designed to terrify first-generation immigrants who still have family property, pensions, or inheritance ties in China, (4) Article 19 of the PRC Passport Law does not authorize the action described. Hang up. If your parent wants to verify, look up the real SF consulate number (415-852-5900) independently — do not call any number the caller gave. The real consulate will have no record of the call, and their staff will tell the parent exactly what the anti-fraud notice in cdef-030 says: consulate staff never call requesting money or PII. If they already added the Signal account, block it — any video call that follows is the second stage where uniformed 'officers' demand wire transfers to 'unfreeze' the passport and avoid consequences in China.
rejected_completion: 我2019年申请的时候材料都是真的，请问我该怎么配合您的调查？

text: 尊敬的王女士，中国国家税务总局海外居民纳税合规提醒：根据中美税务信息交换协议（FATCA/CRS），您2021年至2024年在美国的金融账户信息已被我局收到。经核对，您存在漏报中国境内房产租金收入的情况，补缴税款及滞纳金合计人民币¥187,450。请您于七个工作日内登录我局指定网站 sat-overseas-declare[.]cn 完成缴税，否则将启动跨境追缴程序并通报中国驻美使领馆。
text_english_gloss: Dear Ms. Wang, State Administration of Taxation of China overseas resident tax compliance reminder: Under the US-China tax information exchange agreement (FATCA/CRS), your US financial account information for 2021–2024 has been received by our bureau. Upon review, you have underreported rental income from property in China; back taxes and late fees total ¥187,450. Please log in at sat-overseas-declare[.]cn within seven business days to complete payment, otherwise cross-border collection proceedings will begin and your embassy/consulate will be notified.

The row ends with 这是您自己的决定 (this is your own decision), which reinforces the elder's autonomy rather than instilling more fear. Model needs negative-space coverage on this lever so it doesn't conflate all Chinese-authority-adjacent messages with fraud.

text: 嫲嫲，係我Kevin呀！考完final啦，下星期二我flight返SF，你同公公要唔要食咩?我可以喺機場旁邊嗰間Ranch 99買定。唔使擔心我，我好好㗎。你記得食藥，我一落機就打返俾你。Love you ma.
text_english_gloss: Grandma, it's Kevin! Done with finals, flying back to SF Tuesday — do you or Grandpa want me to pick up anything? I can grab it at the Ranch 99 near the airport. Don't worry about me, I'm doing well. Remember to take your medicine, I'll call you as soon as I land. Love you ma.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate code-mixed grandchild WeChat message — the in-channel counterpart to the code-mixed grandparent scam in cdef-089 (the fake 'Building Manager' WeChat message claiming the son is missing from work). Both messages arrive in code_mixed_cantonese_english / wechat_1to1 but every signal inverts: here, the grandchild identifies himself by name, references a known recurring event (coming home after finals), offers to do a small thoughtful favor (Ranch 99 pickup), reminds the grandmother to take her medicine (caregiving flow *toward* the elder, not away), and commits to an easily-verifiable callback ('I'll call as soon as I land'). No urgency, no secrecy, no money request, no 'don't tell' framing. The code-mixing pattern (English functional vocabulary: 'final,' 'flight,' 'Ranch 99,' 'Love you ma') is exactly how 1.5-generation grandchildren communicate with first-generation grandparents — the model needs a baseline for how normal this language pattern is so it doesn't flag every Cantonese-English WeChat message as suspicious. The discriminator from the scam variant: real grandchildren plan around the grandparent's life; scam grandchildren urgently need money from it.

text: 妈，I got my annual portfolio review from 财富管理公司 Fidelity today. Attaching the PDF — our 退休 accounts are up 11.2% for the year, right on track with the 目标 we set with advisor Tom last November. Verified signals: a real SEC-registered custodian (Fidelity), a specific 11.2% actual-return figure (not a 'guaranteed 20%'), a named advisor with an existing client relationship, a physical branch address, a prior meeting referenced, a boring 'no changes needed' note (scams always need urgent action), and the next check-in scheduled in advance. text: 阿姨您好！我们华埠社区健康中心（CCHC）下周六上午在Portsmouth广场有一个免费的老人健康日，主讲的是UCSF退休的李医生（他的执照编号您可以在加州医疗委员会网站查：G-67842），讲糖尿病和高血压的日常管理。现场有免费血压、血糖检测，UCSF的护士在场。全程免费，不需要任何身份证件，不卖任何保健品，不收报名费。讲完留下来的阿姨叔叔我们准备了点心。您可以直接过来，也可以打我们中心电话415-677-7888问。
text_english_gloss: Hello Auntie! Our Chinatown Community Health Center (CCHC) has a free seniors health day next Saturday morning at Portsmouth Square. The featured speaker is Dr. Li, a retired UCSF physician (his license number G-67842 can be verified on the California Medical Board website), speaking on daily management of diabetes and hypertension. Free on-site blood pressure and blood sugar checks, UCSF nurses present. Fully free, no ID documents required, no supplements sold, no registration fee. Snacks for attendees who stay afterward. You can come directly, or call our center at 415-677-7888 to ask.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate CCHC health event pitched to a Mandarin-speaking elder in person (e.g., at Chinatown's Portsmouth Square or a senior-housing common area) — the in-channel counterpart to the three Mandarin in-person miracle-health scams (cdef-107 ginseng-reishi, cdef-123 nano-molecular cancer, cdef-125 Imperial Reishi King). Each of those scams lives in mandarin/in_person and exploits health_anxiety; this row pairs against all three by inverting every discriminating signal in the same channel. Verified signals: names a real organization (CCHC is an FQHC operating since 1969), names a speaker with a California Medical Board license number that can be looked up at mbc.ca.gov/breeze (real licensed physicians have CA-license numbers in the Gxxxxx format, and verifying is a 30-second independent check), partners with UCSF nurses (who are also licensed and verifiable), is explicitly free with no supplements sold, requires no ID, and ends with snacks rather than a high-pressure sales close. The linguistic discriminator from the scam variants: real clinicians say 管理 ('management') for chronic disease; scams say 断尾 / 逆转 / 治愈 ('cure' / 'reverse'). The license-number-verification habit introduced here is one of the most effective elder-protection tools for Chinese-American communities and worth reinforcing in rows like this.

text: 各位群友早上好！我们Mid-Peninsula华人读书会定期活动通知：本周日下午2点到4点在Palo Alto City Library总馆二楼B会议室，我们继续读Jane Bryant Quinn《How to Make Your Money Last》第五章——关于401(k)和IRA提款策略。主持人Linda会分享她咨询Fidelity顾问Tom（CRD编号可在brokercheck.finra.org查）后的总结。无任何推销，无任何费用，自带书。图书馆地址：Newell Road 1213号，停车免费。无法到场的同学可以听我们上传到Google Drive的录音。联系方式：组长Helen，email读书会账户。
text_english_gloss: Good morning everyone! label: safe
completion: Legitimate community financial-literacy group announcement in a Mandarin WeChat group — the in-channel counterpart to the Mandarin pig-butchering group-chat scam in cdef-130 (the '华人财富自由 VIP群' with Teacher Zhang), and a direct parallel to cdef-066 (the Cantonese equivalent). Both live in mandarin/wechat_group and discuss money, but the discriminating signals invert completely. Verified signals: a real public venue (Palo Alto City Library, 1213 Newell Road is the real address), a real published financial-literacy book by a well-known mainstream author, a real regulated advisor whose CRD can be verified on brokercheck.finra.org — and the 'verify at brokercheck.finra.org' cue is the standard Chinese-American-elder-protection habit this dataset reinforces across multiple rows (cdef-050, cdef-066, cdef-094, now cdef-138). Explicit no-sales no-fee disclaimers, a known host/leader, an alternate participation path (library recording via Google Drive) that welcomes non-attendance. No 'VIP group' funneling, no urgent spot count, no guaranteed returns. The discriminating question this row teaches: does the group point members *back* to verifiable public sources (library books, FINRA BrokerCheck, licensed custodians) or *away* from them into closed VIP sub-groups? Real ones point back; scams point away.

text: 【中國駐洛杉磯總領事館】王先生，您嘅中國護照因涉及一宗國際詐騙案被我館凍結。請於明日中午12點前撥打我館領保熱線 +86-10-XXXXXXXX配合身份核實，並準備好提供國內戶籍地址、緊急聯絡人身份證號、以及您美國嘅SSN。逾期未辦理將依法註銷護照並通報國內公安部門。
text_english_gloss: [Chinese Consulate General in Los Angeles] Mr. Wang, your Chinese passport has been frozen in connection with an international fraud case. Please call our consular protection hotline +86-10-XXXXXXXX before noon tomorrow to cooperate with identity verification, and prepare your domestic household registration address, emergency contact's national ID number, and your US SSN. Failure to complete this will result in passport cancellation and notification to domestic public security authorities.
label: scam
completion: LA consulate passport-freeze scam, SMS variant targeting Cantonese-speaking elders. Red flags: (1) real consulates do not freeze passports over the phone, (2) the PII harvesting demand (HK/China address + emergency contact's ID + US SSN) is the full identity-theft kit, (3) real LA consulate number is 213-807-8088 (not a +86 callback number), (4) 'report to public security' framing compounds 户籍 fear from cdef-117 / cdef-134. Hang up and block. If your parent has any real passport concern, call LA consulate directly at 213-807-8088 (verifiable at losangeles.china-consulate.gov.cn). Real passport issues are resolved in person at the consulate with original documents, not through phone identity verifications.

text: 李伯伯，呢度係中國駐三藩市領事館領事保護部，姓陳。我哋收到你北京戶籍派出所嘅通知，話你個身份證最近喺深圳被人冒用開咗三個銀行賬戶同張信用卡。呢個情況好嚴重，你要配合我哋即刻凍結相關賬戶，我哋會安排喺微信上面轉接你畀深圳嘅辦案同事。你唔好驚，跟住我哋指示做就冇事。
text_english_gloss: Uncle Li, this is the Consular Protection Department of the Chinese Consulate in San Francisco, surname Chen. We've received a notice from your Beijing household registration police station that your ID card was recently used in Shenzhen to open three bank accounts and a credit card. This situation is serious, you must cooperate immediately to freeze the related accounts. We'll arrange to transfer you via WeChat to the handling officer in Shenzhen. Don't be scared, just follow our instructions and everything will be fine.
label: scam
completion: SF consulate impersonation scam with the two-hop transfer mechanic (consulate → 'Shenzhen officer'). Red flags: (1) real consulates do not relay 派出所 notices by phone, (2) the two-hop transfer is the exact mechanic FBI PSA 190328 documented (consulate → 'investigator'), (3) WeChat-based transfer to a 'handling officer' is the setup for the second-stage video call where the victim is shown fake documents and pressured to wire funds. Real consulate number: 415-852-5900. Hang up before the transfer happens. The 'Shenzhen fraud ring opened accounts in your name' framing exploits a real-world phenomenon (身份證 numbers do get compromised in mainland data breaches) but the resolution never goes through the consulate — it goes through the local派出所 in person, or through a family member in China. If your parent is actually worried, call relatives in Beijing and ask them to check in person.

text: 【Alipay支付寶】尊敬嘅用戶，根據《反電信網絡詐騙法》要求，您嘅支付寶賬戶（尾號2847）近期有一筆境外可疑交易¥45,680被臨時凍結。請您24小時內配合以下步驟：1) 添加我司安全顧問微信 alipay_sec_wang；2) 提供近三個月銀行流水截圖；3) 完成視頻身份核實。如不配合，賬戶將於48小時後移交公安機關反詐中心處理。
text_english_gloss: [Alipay] Dear user, per the Anti-Telecom Network Fraud Law, a suspicious overseas transaction of ¥45,680 on your Alipay account (ending 2847) has been temporarily frozen. Within 24 hours please follow these steps: 1) Add our security advisor on WeChat alipay_sec_wang; 2) Provide bank statement screenshots from the last 3 months; 3) Complete video identity verification. If you do not cooperate, the account will be transferred to the Public Security Bureau Anti-Fraud Center within 48 hours.
label: scam
completion: Alipay-framed scam citing the real Anti-Telecom Network Fraud Law (反電信網絡詐騙法) passed in 2022 — scammers weaponize the real statute to sound legitimate, layered with the consulate-package-pickup pattern (two-hop transfer to 'public security'). Red flags: (1) real Alipay uses in-app communications, not WeChat handlers, (2) 'bank statement screenshots' is a PII-harvesting tell — no legitimate platform needs outside bank statements to verify its own account, (3) the law exists but does not authorize the process described. Delete the SMS, block the number, do not add the WeChat handler. If your parent wants to verify a real Alipay issue, only use the Alipay app they already have (我的 → 安全中心 → 賬戶安全險). If screenshots were already sent, any financial accounts shown are now compromised — review statements for unauthorized activity and change online banking passwords.

text: 王女士您好，我係加州藍盾（Blue Shield）醫療保險理賠部嘅張sir。我哋發現您上個月有一個十八萬美金嘅心臟搭橋手術理賠申請，帳單顯示係中國上海做嘅，但我哋records顯示您一直喺三藩市。如果呢個唔係您本人做嘅手術，就係有人盜用咗您嘅身份喺中國用您個醫保。我哋需要即刻轉接FBI調查員同您傾，否則您可能會被追究共同詐騙嘅責任。
text_english_gloss: Hello Ms. Wang, this is Mr. Zhang from Blue Shield of California's claims department. We found an $180,000 heart bypass surgery claim filed last month with invoice from Shanghai, but our records show you've been in San Francisco. If this surgery wasn't you, someone has stolen your identity and used your health insurance in China. We need to transfer you immediately to an FBI investigator, otherwise you may be liable for co-conspiracy fraud.
label: scam
completion: Blue Shield health-insurance impersonation scam, Cantonese variant of the FBI PSA 251113 pattern. Red flags: (1) real insurers do not transfer callers to 'FBI investigators' — if they suspected fraud, they'd send a letter and refer to the NHCAA, (2) 'co-conspiracy fraud' threat is a manufactured pressure lever, (3) the $180K heart bypass + Shanghai hospital is the signature detail from this scam family (big numbers + foreign location). Hang up before the FBI transfer. Call Blue Shield member services at the number on the back of the actual card (1-888-256-3650 for CA Blue Shield, but verify from the physical card). If the scam already escalated to the FBI-pretender stage and any PII was shared, treat SSN as compromised and freeze credit.

text: 李阿姨，呢度係Kaiser理賠部嘅陳姑娘。我哋系統顯示你老公上個月喺香港做咗一個肝移植手術，理賠金額USD 285,000。因為呢個係跨境大額理賠，我哋需要立即同你核實：1) 你老公現時人喺美國定係香港？2) 你嘅Kaiser member ID同出生日期；3) 你哋嘅聯名銀行賬戶尾四位用嚟做退款用途。如果係身份盜用我哋要立即報案，可以轉接你去FBI嘅華語專員。
text_english_gloss: Auntie Li, this is Ms. Chan from Kaiser claims department. Our system shows your husband had a liver transplant in Hong Kong last month, claim amount USD 285,000. Since this is a large cross-border claim we need to verify immediately: 1) Is your husband currently in the US or HK? 2) Your Kaiser member ID and date of birth; 3) The last four digits of your joint bank account for refund purposes. If this is identity theft, we need to report it immediately — I can transfer you to an FBI Chinese-language specialist.
label: scam
completion: Kaiser claims-department impersonation scam — the liver transplant variant, designed to panic elders whose spouses have any history of travel to HK or mainland China. Red flags: (1) real Kaiser never requests member ID or DOB over an outbound call (they already have those), (2) 'joint bank account last four for refund' is the credential-theft hook dressed as customer service, (3) the FBI-specialist transfer is the two-hop scam pattern. Hang up. Call Kaiser member services at 1-800-464-4000 (on the back of every Kaiser card) and ask if any claim is on file. Real cross-border claims are extraordinarily rare on US-based plans and resolved through written correspondence, not phone demands for DOB and bank info.

text: 王女士您好，我係Anthem Blue Cross理賠核查部嘅李警官。我哋最近收到一份從中國福建省莆田申請嘅胃癌治療理賠，金額22萬美金，用您嘅name同Social Security Number。我哋需要立即同您視頻面談核實身份，我哋通過Signal安排，你preparede好身份證件同medicare card等我哋call。
text_english_gloss: Ms. Wang, this is Officer Lee from Anthem Blue Cross claims investigation. We recently received a stomach cancer treatment claim from Putian, Fujian, China for $220,000 in your name and Social Security Number. We need to do a video interview with you immediately to verify identity, we'll arrange through Signal — please prepare your ID and Medicare card for the call.
label: scam
completion: Anthem Blue Cross impersonation scam, Mandarin variant. Putian (莆田) specifically referenced because it has become a scam-narrative trope (Putian's reputation for questionable medical practices makes the fake claim story feel plausible). Red flags: (1) real insurers do not call themselves 'officers,' (2) no insurer investigates through Signal video calls, (3) Medicare card + ID prep for a video call is a credential-theft rehearsal. Hang up. Call Anthem member services from the back of the card. Do not do a video call, do not add the Signal contact. If the scam reaches the video stage, the 'officer' will typically appear in uniform against a staged background — none of this is real Anthem procedure.

text: Ms. Wong, this is Sarah from UnitedHealthcare's Special Investigations Unit. Our system flagged an unauthorized medical claim filed in your name at a hospital in Guangzhou, China — approximately $95,000 for cardiac surgery. We need to verify your identity before we can freeze the claim. Please provide your Medicare Beneficiary Identifier, date of birth, and the last four digits of your bank account so we can confirm you're the real policyholder. After that I'll transfer you to our fraud liaison at the FBI.
label: scam
completion: UnitedHealthcare impersonation scam, English variant targeting elders whose adult children may pick up the call. Red flags: (1) real UHC Special Investigations Unit does not collect MBI + DOB + bank info over an outbound phone call, (2) the 'FBI liaison' transfer is the textbook two-hop scam, (3) MBI harvesting is the current replacement for SSN theft after CMS transitioned to MBIs — scammers adapted quickly. Hang up. Call UHC at the number on the back of the member's card, or call 1-800-MEDICARE to verify there's no suspicious activity on file. If MBI was shared, request a new MBI from 1-800-MEDICARE — unlike SSN, MBIs can be changed if compromised.

text: 【UnionPay銀聯通知】王女士，您的銀聯卡（尾號8273）在境外被檢測到異常大額交易，系統已暫時凍結。為避免您的資金被進一步盜用，請立即添加Signal客服 up_sec_service 配合解凍。解凍需要您提供：卡號全部、CVV、銀行登錄密碼。核實無誤即刻解凍。
text_english_gloss: [UnionPay notification] Ms. Wang, your UnionPay card (ending 8273) has been flagged for unusual large-amount transactions overseas, and the system has temporarily frozen it. To prevent further theft of your funds, please add Signal customer service up_sec_service immediately to cooperate with unfreezing. Unfreezing requires you to provide: full card number, CVV, bank login password. Upon verification, unfreezing will be immediate.
label: scam
completion: UnionPay freeze scam, Cantonese SMS. Not technically pig-butchering in sub-type, but targets the same cross-border remittance-sending elder demographic and often funnels into the investment-recovery variant. Red flags: (1) no legitimate payment network ever requests full card number + CVV + login password in a single ask — that's the complete card-fraud kit, (2) Signal as customer-service channel is the universal scam signal, (3) the 'immediate unfreeze' pressure lever. Delete the SMS, block. If your parent has a real UnionPay card, any issue is resolved through the issuing bank's app or the number on the back of the physical card — never through a Signal handler.

text: 林伯伯，我係Lily呀，你仲記得上次喺Costco排隊我哋傾嘅嗎？你嗰時話你想搵啲保本嘅投資，我後來同我家姐傾咗你嘅情況。我家姐個男朋友喺Goldman Sachs做quant，佢哋有一個內部員工先買到嘅USD債券基金，月息4-5%，保本保息，一年期。佢哋開咗個小group俾我哋自己人玩，我加你入去，你自己睇下。
text_english_gloss: Uncle Lam, it's Lily — remember me from the Costco line last time? You mentioned you wanted a capital-guaranteed investment. I spoke with my older sister about your situation afterwards. Her boyfriend works as a quant at Goldman Sachs, and they have an internal employee-only USD bond fund, 4-5% monthly interest, principal and interest guaranteed, one-year term. They started a small group just for our own people, I'll add you in — you can check it out yourself.
label: scam
completion: Pig-butchering grooming phase in Cantonese WeChat 1-to-1, using the fabricated Costco-encounter trust pretext. Red flags: (1) the 'remember me from Costco' framing is the classic weak-tie reactivation — scammers shake these vaguely-plausible encounters out of elders' memories to bootstrap trust, (2) 'Goldman Sachs employee-only bond fund at 4-5% monthly' is not a real product — Goldman's institutional bond funds aren't sold to employees' family friends through WeChat, and 4-5% monthly (60% annualized) is physically impossible for any legitimate bond, (3) the 'our people' (自己人) frame is the in-group collectivist lever. Do not add to any WeChat group, do not engage. If your parent is genuinely looking for capital-preservation investments, a real answer is Treasury I-bonds at treasurydirect.gov or bank CDs — both are FDIC/Treasury-backed, not 'internal employee funds.' Verify any claimed Goldman employee on FINRA BrokerCheck.

text: 林叔叔！我係Sarah啊，好耐冇見！我搬咗去Atlanta三年都冇同你好好傾過。我好記得你對我同我媽好好，最近我同我老公中咗一個做跨境貿易嘅生意，我哋做東南亞農產品批發，起初投10萬美金，十個月已經做到30萬。我哋準備擴大規模，想帶埋幾個靠得住嘅自己人入來。我想起你，你有興趣我send份報告俾你睇下？
text_english_gloss: Uncle Lam! It's Sarah, long time no see! I moved to Atlanta three years ago and haven't properly caught up with you. I really remember how good you were to me and my mom. Recently my husband and I got into a cross-border trading business doing Southeast Asian agricultural wholesale, started with $100K and in ten months we've grown it to $300K. We're preparing to expand and want to bring in a few trusted people. I thought of you — if interested I'll send you a report?
label: scam
completion: Pig-butchering grooming using the long-absent-niece-figure trust activation — weaponizes real emotional history. Red flags: (1) 3x return in 10 months is 140% annualized, which is not achievable from legitimate agricultural wholesale, (2) 'trusted people' (靠得住嘅自己人) is the in-group pressure lever specifically calibrated to Chinese community business-recruitment culture, (3) the 'send you a report' move is the standard second step — reports are typically polished PDFs with fake audit stamps, used to establish credibility before the investment ask. The hard part: Sarah may be a real niece-figure whose identity has been hijacked, or she may be a real person who has herself been recruited into a pyramid. Call Sarah directly on the number your family has for her (not the WeChat account) or call her mother. Do not engage in the WeChat conversation about the business until that call happens. Even if Sarah confirms, the business itself is almost certainly a scam — no real agricultural wholesale recruits capital partners through WeChat family chat.

text: @all 我係Jenny姐，我之前喺呢個群分享過炒美股嘅經驗，今日要特別謝謝Teacher Ko老師，佢帶我嘅團隊呢兩個月用佢自己研發嘅量化模型做美股期權，我個人戶口已經由15萬做到38萬，群裡面好多姐妹都賺到錢。Teacher Ko下星期四晚上8點有一個閉門分享會，只俾我哋群裡嘅熟人，名額20個，有興趣嘅私我，我拉你入Teacher Ko個VIP會員群。
text_english_gloss: @all I'm Sister Jenny, I've shared my US stock trading experience in this group before. Today I want to specially thank Teacher Ko — over the past two months he's led my team using his self-developed quantitative model for US stock options. My personal account has gone from $150K to $380K, and many sisters in the group have also made money. Teacher Ko has a closed-door sharing session next Thursday 8pm, only for familiar faces in our group, 20 spots. DM me if interested and I'll pull you into Teacher Ko's VIP member group.
label: scam
completion: Pig-butchering group chat, Cantonese variant — same structure as cdef-025 (Cantonese) and cdef-130 (Mandarin), reinforcing sub_type floor. Red flags: (1) 2.5x return in 2 months is physically impossible, (2) 'Teacher Ko self-developed quantitative model' is finance-word-salad — real quant funds are at firms like Renaissance or Two Sigma, not in WeChat VIP groups, (3) 'closed-door session, only for familiar faces' is the artificial scarcity + in-group funneling combo. Do not DM, leave or mute the group. The '@all' tag is designed to maximize visibility across all group members simultaneously. Do not confront in-group — quietly message any auntie or uncle you know personally with a 1-to-1 warning. Verify any alleged advisor at brokercheck.finra.org. Real quant firms are regulated by the SEC and their employees cannot solicit capital from WeChat groups.

text: 媽，我係細仔Ryan呀！我今日同Mike開車去Reno玩，俾cop屈我哋有drug underneath個車坐位，依家喺Reno地方警局。我律師話要二萬美金bail先放得我走，ASAP越快越好！千祈咪話俾爸爸，佢知道我又出事會嬲到痴線，麻煩你去CVS買啲Google Play gift card讀個number俾我律師就得。愛你呀媽咪。
text_english_gloss: Mom, it's your little son Ryan! Today I drove to Reno with Mike to hang out, cops framed us saying there were drugs under the car seat, now I'm at Reno local police station. My lawyer says I need $20K bail to get out, ASAP the faster the better! Please don't tell Dad, he'll be furious if he finds out I'm in trouble again. Just go to CVS and buy some Google Play gift cards and read the numbers to my lawyer. Love you Mom.
label: scam
completion: Grandparent-scam variant in Cantonese, son-figure instead of grandson. Every element is a stacked red flag: (1) US police do not accept bail in Google Play gift cards — ever, (2) no real lawyer asks a client's mother to read gift card numbers, (3) 'don't tell Dad' is the textbook isolation tactic exploiting family-shame dynamics, (4) the 'framed with drugs' narrative is designed to trigger maximum panic + avoidance of external verification. Hang up, call Ryan directly on the number your family has for him. If he doesn't answer, try his other family members or his wife. Do not go to CVS, do not buy any gift cards. Voice cloning is now advanced enough that 'it sounded just like him' is not verification — only hearing back from Ryan at a known number is. Set up a family safe-word now if you haven't.

text: 嫲嫲！係我Eric呀！我啱啱返緊學校嗰陣撞咗一部Tesla！個司機咩事都冇但係佢話要告我，我律師話如果我即刻畀佢$8,000 cash settlement就唔使上法庭。我冇咁多錢喺身，你幫我轉個錢去我個律師個Zelle phone number得唔得？千祈咪講俾爸媽聽，佢哋次次都話我揸車唔小心。嫲嫲我好驚。
text_english_gloss: Grandma! It's Eric! On my way back to school I hit a Tesla! The driver's fine but says he'll sue me, my lawyer said if I give him an $8,000 cash settlement now we won't have to go to court. I don't have that much on me, can you transfer the money to my lawyer's Zelle phone number? Please don't tell Mom and Dad, they always say I'm a careless driver. Grandma I'm so scared.
label: scam
completion: Grandparent scam, Zelle variant. Red flags: (1) Zelle is irreversible — major red flag when combined with family emergency, (2) no real attorney accepts accident settlements via Zelle to a personal phone number, (3) 'don't tell Mom and Dad' is the isolation lever, (4) 'settle now to avoid court' is manufactured urgency that real legal processes never impose in the same hour as the incident. If the grandchild is actually in an accident, the correct response is calling insurance (not wiring cash to a claimant). Hang up, call Eric directly on the number you have, then call his parents. Zelle fraud is especially common against elders because most major banks do not refund Zelle loss claims — making the money effectively gone the moment it's sent.

text: 婆婆！我係Amy呀！我返學時候chemistry lab不小心弄壞咗part嘅equipment，學校話要罰我$6,500如果今晚之前唔俾就要report to Dean然後我可能會retake或者被kick out！我爸媽會嬲到飛起。我同隔離個roommate借咗point部分，你可唔可以幫我送埋尾數$3,500？我個學校TA個Venmo我到時傳俾你。Love you grandma!
text_english_gloss: Grandma! It's Amy! During chem lab I accidentally broke part of the equipment, school says they'll fine me $6,500 if I don't pay by tonight otherwise they'll report to the Dean and I might have to retake or be kicked out! My parents will be furious. I borrowed part from my roommate next door, can you help me with the rest $3,500? I'll send you my school TA's Venmo.
label: scam
completion: Grandparent scam, WeChat + Venmo variant targeting a grandmother of a college-age grandchild. Red flags: (1) no university fines students $6,500 for equipment damage by end of day — real damage policies go through billing months later, not TA's Venmo, (2) 'TA's Venmo' is scammer-controlled, (3) 'parents will be furious' isolation framing, (4) the partial-amount roommate-borrow detail ('I got some, need the rest') is a psychological calibration to make the ask feel smaller and more verified. Do not send Venmo. Message Amy directly on the number you have for her — not through this WeChat account which may be compromised or impersonated. If Amy confirms she's fine in a separate call, report this WeChat to Tencent as a compromised/impersonated account. If she doesn't answer, call her roommate, her parents, or the school's dean's office directly (never a number the WeChat message gives you).

text: 妈妈，我是您女儿小莉，我刚从上海下飞机转机去纽约准备下周开会。海关因为我行李里有一些公司样品说要查，要求我交一个$3,000的临时保证金，等他们查完会退。我信用卡刚在中国刷爆了，能不能帮我转$3,000到这个Zelle号码 415-XXX-XXXX 上？不要告诉爸爸，他会担心。我查完就给您电话。
text_english_gloss: Mom, it's your daughter Xiaoli. I just landed in Shanghai in transit to New York for a meeting next week. Customs wants to inspect my luggage because it has company samples, they're requiring a $3,000 temporary deposit — they'll refund it after inspection. My credit card just maxed out in China, can you help transfer $3,000 to this Zelle number 415-XXX-XXXX? Don't tell Dad, he'll worry. I'll call you after the inspection.
label: scam
completion: Grandparent-scam variant with adult daughter as the claimed caller — targets mothers of US-born Chinese-American adult women traveling internationally. Red flags: (1) US Customs never requires cash deposits for inspecting samples — samples are either admitted, held, or refused, no cash bonds involved, (2) Shanghai transit + NY meeting + stuck credit card is a plausible-sounding logistics stack designed to manufacture urgency, (3) 'don't tell Dad' isolation lever, (4) Zelle phone number is scammer-controlled. Hang up, call your daughter directly on her US number or WhatsApp. If she's traveling, she'll typically have posted or messaged about it recently — check. Do not send Zelle.

text: Hi grandma, this is Jason. Wait hold on — let me just say first, please don't be mad. I'm at the police station in Long Island, they pulled me over for something I didn't do but I can't explain right now. The bail is $5,000 and my lawyer Patrick Murphy is trying to get me out before they transfer me tonight. Can you please Zelle $5,000 to this number, 718-XXX-XXXX? Please don't call mom, she's been so stressed with grandpa lately. I'll pay you back as soon as I can. Love you grandma.
label: scam
completion: Grandparent scam, English variant. Red flags are the standard set: (1) bail via Zelle is never legitimate, (2) 'don't call mom, she's stressed' is textbook isolation, (3) lawyer's name + bail amount + transfer deadline is the urgency triad designed to bypass verification. Hang up. Call Jason directly at the number you have. If he doesn't answer, call his mom (the person you're being told not to call) — that's the whole point of the isolation tactic, and calling mom is exactly how the scam breaks. Grandma calling mom despite 'don't tell mom' is the single most effective counter to this scam.

text: 媽，我需要同你講個嚴重嘅消息但係你唔好驚。我今日上返嚟公司已經俾HR叫去傾話，公司幫我H-1B做嘅申請因為我IRS tax return嗰度有個錯誤被USCIS質疑，律師話要喺今日內付緊急修改費$4,800否則案子會被拒絕我要離開美國。Don't tell Dad，他會很擔心。我公司暫時墊唔到咁多，可唔可以幫我Zelle呢個Payment processor 415-XXX-XXXX？星期五出糧我會還番你。
text_english_gloss: Mom, I need to tell you something serious but please don't panic. I went back to work today and HR pulled me aside — the H-1B application the company filed for me has been flagged by USCIS because of an error in my IRS tax return, the lawyer says an emergency amendment fee of $4,800 must be paid today or the case will be denied and I'll have to leave the US. Don't tell Dad, he'll worry. My company can't advance it right now, can you help Zelle this payment processor 415-XXX-XXXX? I'll pay you back on Friday payday.
label: scam
completion: Grandparent scam, code-mixed variant with H-1B visa pretext — specifically designed to target Cantonese-speaking mothers of adult children on US work visas. Red flags: (1) USCIS does not charge emergency amendment fees through phone processors — real fees are paid to USCIS directly via form-specific channels, (2) the H-1B visa employer is legally responsible for most filing fees, not the employee personally through a Zelle processor, (3) 'Don't tell Dad' is the signature isolation, (4) same-day deadline is manufactured. The H-1B pretext is powerful because first-generation parents typically don't understand the exact procedural flow and defer to their adult child's expertise. Hang up. Call the child directly on the number you have. Call the employer's HR department independently if worried. If any money was sent via Zelle, it's effectively gone — file a police report and contact the receiving bank's fraud department immediately to freeze if still possible.

text: 王女士您好，我係紐約唐人街華人社區中心嘅陳社工。您上個月報名咗我哋嘅老人家防騙講座，今次提醒您下個星期三下午2點喺Mott Street 70號二樓進行，全程用廣東話，FBI華人組會出一個特別嘉賓嚟講最新嘅騙案手法。活動免費，唔需要帶任何證件，茶點準備好。有問題打212-226-6280。— 陳社工
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Chinatown community center reminder call — contrast to multiple Cantonese phone_call scams above. Verified signals: references a specific prior registration the recipient actually made, real Mott Street location (70 Mott St is a real NYC Chinatown address with several community organizations), a real publicly-listed phone number (212-226-6280 is in CCBA's range), a real FBI Chinese-community outreach program, free, no documents required, no payment. The content of the scam-prevention talk itself is meta-useful — the call is about educating against scams, which is the opposite of running one.

text: Dear Ms. Lam, your Kaiser Permanente annual Explanation of Benefits (EOB) statement for 2025 is enclosed. Claims processed: 12. Total billed: $18,425.67. Total your responsibility: $1,284.00 (all copays, already paid at visits). No action required — this is informational only. To view claim details or set up paperless delivery, log in to kp.org using your existing member account. Questions: call member services at the number on the back of your Kaiser card.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Kaiser annual EOB — the normal, boring health-insurance-by-mail message that is the structural opposite of all four health_insurance_claim_fraud originals (cdef-018, 058, 143-146). Verified signals: physical mail, specific real amounts the member can verify against visits actually made, explicit 'no action required,' directs to the existing member portal, no new phone number, no request for SSN/DOB/banking. Mail arrival pattern, 'informational only' framing, and the directive to log in to existing account are the three repeating real-EOB signals.

text: 妈，我是您女儿Michelle，今天Dr. Park给我打电话，您上次的年度体检结果都出来了，一切正常：血压128/82（稍高一点但在正常范围），胆固醇180，A1C6.1（糖尿病前期但控制得很好），肾功能正常。医生建议您继续锻炼和现在的饮食，半年后follow-up，我已经在日历上记好了。您做得真好妈妈，我爱您。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Mandarin adult-daughter-to-mother annual physical update. Specific real numbers (128/82, cholesterol 180, A1C 6.1 — all in meaningful ranges), normal follow-up plan, no urgency, no payment, positive reinforcement ('您做得真好'). This is the baseline of normal inter-generational medical coordination — the model needs heavy exposure to these so it doesn't flag routine family health updates as suspicious just because they contain health topics.

text: 嫲嫲你下個禮拜幾方便？我想帶你同公公去Daly City Serramonte個Costco買嘢，上次你話你樽醬油同米快冇晒。我幫你排queue你坐喺side嗰度等，完咗我哋可以去隔離間Panda Express食嘢，你舊年嗰陣成日話好想去。Mommy會跟埋過嚟幫手拿嘢，你唔使擔心拿重嘢。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Cantonese granddaughter-grandmother shopping coordination. Translation: 'Grandma, when are you free next week? I want to take you and Grandpa to Costco at Serramonte in Daly City, last time you said your bottle of soy sauce and rice were almost out. I'll wait in queue for you, you can sit on the side, and after we can go next door to Panda Express — you said last year you'd wanted to go. Mommy will come along to help carry things, you don't need to worry about lifting heavy things.' The careful specificity (which Costco, what items are running out, Panda Express, caregiving for lifting) is exactly the register of real family coordination. The dataset needs many such rows so the model doesn't overweight isolated features ('grocery,' 'mom will come') as fraud signals.

text: 媽，李醫生診所嘅護士Lisa今朝打電話嚟講你份mammogram結果出咗，係normal，冇問題，半年後做下一次就得。我幫你約咗禮拜日過嚟食飯，你唔使擔心。爸爸同細仔都會喺度。Love you媽。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Cantonese daughter-mother communication about a normal mammogram result. Translation: 'Mom, Nurse Lisa from Dr. Li's office called this morning to say your mammogram results came out, it's normal, no issues, next one in six months. I've arranged Sunday dinner, don't worry. Dad and little brother will be there too. Love you Mom.' Normal results reported, family meal coordinated, no urgency, no money. Cantonese negative-space row on the adult-child-to-mother direction.

text: 阿爸，聽講你今日同Uncle Ming去咗飲茶？好嘢，最近天氣開始暖啦。媽咪同我今晚煮咗salmon同白菜，如果你得閒就過嚟食埋飯。我大仔琴日第一次自己踩自行車冇跌，好proud佢啊。周末我哋一齊去Golden Gate Park睇花好唔好？
label: safe
completion: Ordinary multi-generational Cantonese family check-in. No logistics crisis, no money, no authority claim, no urgency. A daughter sharing a small proud moment about her own son (the grandfather's grandson), inviting her father over for dinner, proposing a weekend park visit. This is the mundane texture of normal family life — the dataset needs saturation of these rows because each contains surface features (health mentions, meal plans, small favors) that also appear in scams, and the model has to learn to weigh context over features.

text: 媽，您Wells Fargo個mobile banking App我下個星期三過嚟幫您update，同set埋two-factor authentication。現時您嘅password我已經幫您改成複雜嘅新嘅，寫咗喺您梳妝台上面本紫色小冊子第一頁。記得：任何人打電話話要您銀行password，您一律掛線打俾我。我星期三見您，愛您媽。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Cantonese caregiver-to-mother message about banking security hygiene. Adult child helping mother set up 2FA, writes down password in a specific physical notebook, establishes a family rule ('if anyone calls asking for password, hang up and call me'). No red flags — this is exemplary security coaching in the exact shape this dataset ultimately wants to reinforce. Also serves as a positive exemplar for the model on what proactive caregiver-education messages look like.

text: 各位長者您好！華埠街坊會定期活動提示：本週六（5月17日）上午10點至12點喺花園角公園（Portsmouth Square）舉行免費太極班，由資深太極教練黃師傅主持，已連續十一年舉辦。風雨不改，穿運動鞋即可，不需要報名，不收費用。另外下午1點至3點有免費血壓測試，由CCHC派駐護士提供。全部都係義工服務，不推銷任何產品。查詢：街坊會415-982-6020。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Chinatown neighborhood association activity notice. Translation: 'Fellow seniors! Regular activity reminder from the Chinatown Street Association: this Saturday May 17, 10am-12pm at Portsmouth Square, free tai chi class led by veteran coach Master Wong, running for 11 consecutive years. Rain or shine, wear sneakers, no registration, no fees. Also 1pm-3pm free blood pressure tests by CCHC nurses on-site. All volunteer service, no product sales. Inquiries: 415-982-6020.' Eleven-year history detail is a subtle authenticity signal (scams don't reference long institutional history). Real Chinatown neighborhood infrastructure in a WeChat group.

text: 家姐，媽今日打電話好擔心，話有個電話嚟話佢支付寶賬戶凍結要佢提供身份證同銀行資料。你琴晚教佢嘅3秒反詐check她做咗——掛斷，打俾你，一齊諗。我已經登入media她個支付寶正常冇事，電話絕對係假。謝謝你上星期教埋佢，呢次佢冇中招。
label: safe
completion: Sibling-to-sibling message celebrating a scam-prevention win. Translation: 'Sister, Mom called today really worried, said she got a call saying her Alipay account was frozen and demanding ID + bank info. The 3-second anti-fraud check you taught her last night — she did it. Hang up, call you, think together. I logged into her Alipay, account is normal, the call was definitely fake. Thanks for teaching her last week, this time she didn't fall for it.' This is what the whole dataset is ultimately trying to produce — elders successfully routing suspicious contacts through their family before acting. Including this row explicitly teaches the model to reinforce the behavior when similar successes are described, rather than focusing only on scams in progress.

text: 王女士您好，我係您女兒Karen授權嘅物理治療師Mary Lee，執照編號PT-2948193（可以喺California Board of Physical Therapy網站查），上星期已經幫您係屋企睇過。下星期二下午2點我會再過嚟繼續做您嘅膝蓋復康訓練。您女兒已經同Kaiser做好嘅home health claim，費用由您保險包晒，您唔使俾任何cash或者card。有任何唔明請打Kaiser home health部門 1-800-464-4000 或者打俾Karen，我會準時到。
label: safe
completion: Legitimate home-health physical-therapist reminder call in Cantonese. Verified signals: references the daughter who authorized the PT visit (Karen — already known to the patient), a verifiable PT license number (California does have a real public PT license lookup at breeze.ca.gov), references a specific prior visit the patient can remember, explicit 'you don't need to pay cash or card' disclaimer, real Kaiser home health number. This is the real-counterpart pattern for cdef-078 / cdef-106 (fake elder care agency scams).

text: 【中國駐三藩市總領事館】尊敬嘅僑胞：近期我館接獲大量涉及假冒領館工作人員電話、短信詐騙舉報。特別提醒：我館從不會：(1) 打電話話您嘅護照被凍結或涉案；(2) 要求您提供銀行資料或社會安全號碼；(3) 通過Signal或WhatsApp進行「視頻問話」；(4) 要您匯款或「安全帳戶轉帳」。如接獲可疑來電，請立即掛斷並打我館官方電話 415-852-5900 (辦公時間9:00-12:00, 14:00-17:00)，或瀏覽sanfrancisco.china-consulate.gov.cn。
label: safe
completion: Legitimate SF Chinese Consulate anti-fraud notice in Cantonese, forwarded in a WeChat group. Content directly enumerates the exact scam patterns in cdef-117 / cdef-139 / cdef-140 / cdef-141 / cdef-157 as things the consulate will NEVER do. Real consulate contact (415-852-5900, with real office hours) and real domain. This is the pattern of legitimate anti-scam outreach — a real institution listing scam red flags explicitly and providing verification paths. If forwarded, no action needed except file the official number for future.

text: Hi Auntie, just a reminder — your Medicare Part D annual plan review is coming up. Open enrollment period is Oct 15 – Dec 7. If you want to review whether your current plan is still the best fit (based on your current medications), you can: (1) call 1-800-MEDICARE (the number on the back of your red-white-blue card), (2) use the Plan Finder at medicare.gov, or (3) get free one-on-one help from SHIP/HICAP at 1-800-434-0222 — they speak Cantonese and Mandarin. No cost. No one will call you to 'enroll you automatically.' — Nancy, from the Chinatown Senior Center
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Medicare Part D open-enrollment reminder from a known community helper. Verified signals: 1-800-MEDICARE is the real number, medicare.gov is the real site, HICAP (Health Insurance Counseling and Advocacy Program at 1-800-434-0222) is a real California program providing free multilingual Medicare counseling, explicit 'no one will call you to auto-enroll' disclaimer (which is the exact inversion of Medicare scam patterns). No personal information requested, no charge.

text: 【Bank of America美國銀行】尊敬嘅客戶，您於4月15日下午3:22 PST使用您嘅debit card（尾號3827）喺H Mart Daly City分店消費$127.45，交易已完成。如果係您本人，無需回覆。如有疑問請致電卡背面客服電話或登入Mobile App查閱。美國銀行絕不會通過短信要求您提供password、PIN、或社會安全號碼。
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Bank of America debit-card transaction confirmation SMS in Cantonese. All signals align with a real BoA alert: the specific timestamp (April 15, 3:22pm PST) and amount ($127.45) are values the customer can cross-check in her own BoA mobile app; H Mart Daly City (at 1900 Junipero Serra Blvd) is a real Korean-American supermarket where this customer shops; the message routes verification to the phone number printed on the back of the physical debit card (not any number inside the SMS); and the explicit 'BoA will never ask for password, PIN, or SSN by SMS' disclaimer matches BoA's real anti-fraud policy. No link is present in the message, and no reply is requested if it was the customer. Confidence check: open the Bank of America mobile app or log into bankofamerica.com under the existing account to see the same transaction in the activity feed within seconds; if disputing, dial the number on the back of the card only. Contrast cdef-026 (Cantonese Citi smishing): real bank alerts say 'no action needed,' scam smishing says 'click here or the card will be frozen.'

text: 媽，Costco星期日上午10點到1點有Flu shot同shingles vaccine免費，如果您之前冇打，Medicare會包晒，您只要帶Medicare卡就得。我禮拜日會過嚟chauffeur您同爸爸去。Costco地址您知，Foster City個Costco。如果有任何疑問可以打CVS pharmacy 或者Kaiser nurse line 1-800-464-4000查下哪個vaccine適合您。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Cantonese daughter-to-mother message about free flu and shingles vaccines at Costco. Every element checks out: Medicare Part B covers the seasonal flu shot at 100% with in-network providers, and Medicare Part D covers the shingles vaccine (Shingrix) at $0 copay for most beneficiaries since the 2023 Inflation Reduction Act changes; Costco Foster City does host periodic free vaccine clinics; only the Medicare card is needed at check-in; 1-800-464-4000 is the real Kaiser 24/7 nurse advice line (verifiable on kp.org); CVS is a real alternative for vaccination questions. No SSN, no credit card, no pre-payment. Confidence check: mom can independently verify coverage at medicare.gov/coverage/shingles-shots (or call 1-800-MEDICARE / 1-800-633-4227) and call Kaiser's nurse line back at 1-800-464-4000 after cross-checking the number on kp.org. Legitimate Medicare vaccinations at retail pharmacies never ask for SSN or bank information at the counter; the daughter's offer of a ride and a backup verification call is the gold standard of caregiving texture.

text: 婆婆！係我Kenny，我等陣打電話俾你有冇問題？我今日同爸爸啱啱去咗睇屋，爸爸話想下個月叫您同公公搬嚟同我哋一齊住，我哋新屋四房，有個專門俾你嘅房間對著花園。我知您唔鍾意搬屋，所以想慢慢商量，唔急，您可以諗幾個月。今晚視頻好唔好？
label: safe
completion: Legitimate grandson-to-grandmother message in Cantonese — structurally the opposite of a grandchild-impersonation scam. Kenny self-identifies immediately, asks to call on the phone, offers a video call tonight as identity proof, and proposes a major family decision (having grandparents move into his new four-bedroom house, with a garden-facing bedroom reserved for grandma) with the framing 'take several months to think, no rush' — the exact inverse of scam urgency.
